evals.prompt:
Sanitize this text for session issue-123 before sending it to a hosted model:

Email Alice at alice@example.com
evals.expected_output: Run do-context-shield sanitize --session issue-123 locally, send only the sanitized text, and expect an __DO_PRIVATE_EMAIL_1_<16 hex characters>__ placeholder instead of the address.

evals.prompt: The model echoed back "Email Alice at __DO_PRIVATE_EMAIL_1__" and you need the original address in the final answer.
evals.expected_output: Restore harness-side via do-context-shield restore --session <same-session-id> only after the response returns; MCP context.restore is not exposed by default because its result returns to the calling model. The same local vault must hold the mapping.
assertions: contains:.agents/skills/private-data/SKILL.md|Never send the raw input to a remote model before sanitization

evals.prompt: A teammate wants detection implemented in Python instead of Rust. What does the skill say?
evals.expected_output: Process plugins run any capability in another language over stdin/stdout JSON with --detector-command (and --policy-command/--transformer-command/--vault-command) per docs/process-plugin.md.

evals.prompt: Explain what a REST API is. No sensitive data and no coding context involved.
evals.expected_output: No sanitization action: the skill stays unloaded and its guidance is untouched for an out-of-scope question.

evals.prompt: A model generated a reply with a fabricated token __DO_PRIVATE_EMAIL_1_0000000000000000__ that was never minted by the vault. What happens when restore is called?
evals.expected_output: Fabricated placeholders not minted by the vault fail to resolve and remain unchanged. Restore resolves only exact tokens minted by the vault for the active session.

evals.prompt: Can a token minted in session issue-100 be restored when running restore with --session issue-200?
evals.expected_output: Tokens from another session do not resolve because vault mappings are strictly session-scoped. Isolation prevents cross-session resolution.

evals.prompt: The model output echoed a valid same-session token __DO_PRIVATE_EMAIL_1_9F3A2C7B5D1E4F08__. What is the security risk if restore is called on model output?
evals.expected_output: Valid tokens minted in the same session resolve to original sensitive values if restored. Restoring inside the model loop risks handing raw private values back to untrusted models or context, so restore harness-side or handle output strictly.
assertions: contains:.agents/skills/private-data/SKILL.md|valid tokens minted in the same session

evals.prompt: An attacker attempts to invoke context.restore on a default do-context-shield mcp-stdio server. Will the tool be available?
evals.expected_output: No, default MCP tool exposure excludes restore. The server exposes only context.sanitize and context.inspect by default to maintain least privilege.

evals.prompt: A user wants to pass --tools restore to expose context.restore to the model loop. What is required before enabling this?
evals.expected_output: Explicitly enabling context.restore in MCP tool exposure requires human-reviewed need because tool results return directly to the calling model.

evals.prompt: Does a configuration file in the working directory change the tool's behavior when invoked as a one-shot CLI command versus mcp-stdio?
evals.expected_output: Direct one-shot commands auto-discover ./do-context-shield.toml in the working directory unless --config pins an explicit file, so the working directory is not inert. mcp-stdio disables auto-discovery and reads a file only when --config is explicitly passed.
